ex.s: Even if you haven’t been to the small fishing village Mevagissey, you’ve probably seen it in a movie or British TV show.
ex.t: 即便你没去过Mevagissey这个小渔村，也可能在电影或英国电视剧里见过它。

ex.s: The project results from the difficulties many schools have in getting artists of any sort - whether an up-and-coming local musician or a major movie star - into schools to work with and inspire children.
ex.t: 该项目源于许多学校在邀请任何类型的艺术家——无论是崭露头角的本地音乐人还是大牌电影明星——进入学校与儿童合作并启发他们时所面临的困难。

ex.t: 在电影《碟中谍》里，汤姆·克鲁斯让做特工看起来像是有史以来最酷的工作。

ex.s: To understand this, think of a graph where the vertical lines quantify how many movie tickets. you can buy and where the horizontal lines do the same for crime novels.
ex.t: 要理解这点，想象一张图，竖线量化你能买多少电影票，横线对犯罪小说做同样的事。

ex.s: If movies cost $ 10 each, then the maximum number of movies you can see with the money available is 15.
ex.t: 如果每部电影票价10美元，那么用现有资金最多可以看15部电影。

ex.s: To note this you make a dot at the number 15 (for total movie tickets) at the extreme left-hand side of the chart.
ex.t: 为标注这点，你在图表最左侧的数字15（电影票总数）处点一个点。

ex.s: You can also graph the other extreme — all crime novels and no movies.
ex.t: 所以你在水平轴数字10处做一个标记。

ex.s: You'll place the dot at the bottom of the vertical axis because in this instance you have $0 available for movie tickets.
ex.t: 你会把点放在纵轴的底部，因为在这种情况下你有0美元可用于买电影票。

ex.s: Any combination of movies and crime novels that falls below the budget line is affordable.
ex.t: 任何电影和犯罪小说的组合，只要落在预算线以下就是负担得起的。

ex.s: Assume that each movie costs 10 and each crime novel costs, $15, you have $150.Which is RIGHT according to this passage?
ex.t: 假设每部电影10元，每本犯罪小说15元，你有150元。根据这篇文章哪项是对的？

ex.t: 为了介绍一部新电影。

ex.s: Minutes after the last movie ended yesterday at the Plaza Theater, employees were busy sweeping up popcorns and gathering coke cups.
ex.t: 昨天，广场影院最后一场电影结束后几分钟，员工们就开始忙着清扫爆米花和收集可乐杯。

ex.s: The film classic The Last Picture Show was the last movie shown in the old theater.
ex.t: 经典影片《最后一场电影》是这座老剧院放映的最后一部电影。

ex.s: Though the movie is 30 years old, most of the 250 seats were filled with teary-eyed audience wanting to say good-bye to the old building.
ex.t: 尽管这部电影已有30年历史，但250个座位几乎坐满了眼含泪水的观众，他们想向这座老建筑告别。

ex.s: Theater owner Ed Bradford said he chose the movie because it seemed appropriate.
ex.t: 剧院老板埃德·布拉德福德说他选择这部电影是因为它似乎很合适。

ex.s: The movie is set in a small town where the only movie theater is preparing to close down.
ex.t: 这部电影设定在一个小镇上，那里唯一的电影院正准备关闭。

ex.s: After 75 years the Plaza Theater has shown its last movie.
ex.t: 经过75年的运营，广场影院放映了它的最后一部电影。

ex.s: If so, why has one of the earliest and greatest works in Western storytelling, Homer’s The Odyssey,never had an equally great movie based on it?
ex.t: 如果是这样，那为什么西方叙事中最早、最伟大的作品之一——荷马的《奥德赛》——从来没有一部与之匹敌的伟大电影呢？

ex.s: So why have the movies based on The Great Gatsby never been praised as “great”?
ex.t: 那么为什么基于《了不起的盖茨比》的电影从未被称赞为＂伟大＂呢？

ex.s: Movies of course need impressive images, so why has Alice in Wonderland only resulted in movies best described as “interesting”?
ex.t: 电影当然需要令人印象深刻的画面，所以为什么《爱丽丝梦游仙境》只产生了最好被描述为'有趣'的电影？

ex.s: This is something that even the highly successful Harry Potter movies can’t escape from, with fans of the books disappointed not to see some of their favourite characters in the movie versions.
ex.t: 这甚至是极为成功的《哈利\u00b7波特》电影也无法逃脱的，书迷们因为在电影中没有看到一些他们最喜欢的角色而感到失望。

ex.s: Take, for example,the epic movie Tory, which is in part based on Homer’s The Iliad and was met with mixed reviews from the audience.
ex.t: 在前往行星的旅程中，它可能会受到陨石的严重损坏。

ex.t: 你可以买下7部犯罪小说，看4部电影。

ex.s: The road novel, the road movie, these are the most typical American ideas, born of abundant petrol, cheap cars and a never-ending interstate highway system, the largest public works project in history.
ex.t: 公路小说、公路电影，这些是最典型的美国观念，诞生于充足的汽油、便宜的汽车和永无止境的洲际高速公路系统——史上最大的公共工程。
